correction.text: unchanged shape, but only for 756: the older papal holdings (the Duchy of Rome); the state begins in 756

keyframe_review.note: 12.8k km2, 755-756: the Duchy of Rome, the older papal holdings to which Pepin's gift was added (Donation of Pepin page, paraphrased). The Papal States page's infobox dates the state 'under the direct sovereign rule of the pope from 756 to 1870', so the shape is drawn from 756, not 755. Cliopatria's allegiance row to the Byzantine Empire (755-869) is not supported by the pages opened: the Donation page says envoys of the Empire offered a large sum to restore the lands and Pepin refused, and that 'the imperial presence in central Italy' was at an end.

21.8k km2, 757-762: Ravenna and the Pentapolis. The Donation page names Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia and Ancona as the five cities, Forlì 'with their hinterlands', and Ravenna as the exarchate; the shape holds Ravenna, Cesena, Forlì, Ancona, Urbino and the Comacchio coast. The page says the boundaries 'can only be approximated, since the text of the treaty has not survived', so the shape is approximate.

27.4k km2, 763-774: adds Bologna, Imola and Ferrara. The Ferrara page dates the pledge of the Lombard 'ducatus ferrariae' to Stephen II to 757; 763 is Cliopatria's year for the wider Emilia, which no page opened dates (ledger confidence 1).

14.1k km2, 775-777: Cliopatria withdraws to the Duchy of Rome after Charlemagne became king of the Lombards in 774. The Donation page says Charlemagne confirmed the Donation (it gives 778, and Louis the Pious in 817) and the Papal States page says some later claimed a 781 extension, so the exarchate stayed a papal claim; the Romagna page says papal control there 'long remained only nominal'. The shape draws effective control only; the claim is carried by soft certainty and a confidence-1 ledger loss.

14.1k km2, 778-782: same shape as 775. The Donation page dates Charlemagne's confirmation of the gift to 778; whether the pope then held Ravenna in fact is not said (the Romagna page: control 'only nominal').

20.2k km2, 783-787: adds a strip of southern Tuscany (the shape's west edge moves to 10.5 E). The Papal States page: 'Some later claimed that in 781' Charlemagne extended papal lands to include parts of Benevento, Tuscany, Corsica and Lombardy; the page presents it as a later claim, so the shape and the 781 event are confidence 2 at best.

Month of the break not given by either page.

29.5k km2, 1860: Lazio, Umbria and most of the Marche (Ancona is out of the shape). The Sardinian army crossed the border on 11 September, won at Castelfidardo on 18 September and Ancona surrendered on 29 September; plebiscites in the Marche and Umbria followed in November 1860 (Castelfidardo page), so the year ends with Lazio alone (the 1861 shape). The ledger carries the months.

14.1k km2, 1861-1869: Lazio, the 'Patrimony' around Rome. Rome was declared the capital of Italy in March 1861 but held by the pope under a French garrison until 1870 (Papal States and Roman Republic 1849 pages).

14.1k km2, 1870: Lazio until the Italian army breached the Aurelian Walls at Porta Pia on 20 September 1870; royal decree of 9 October 1870 confirmed the incorporation after the 2 October plebiscite (Capture of Rome page).

region.text: the Duchy of Rome and the older papal holdings

ledger.note: 756: Pepin's gift makes the pope a temporal sovereign. The infobox: 'under the direct sovereign rule of the pope from 756 to 1870'; the Donation of Pepin gave Pope Stephen II lands formerly held by Arian Lombards, which were added to older papal holdings (paraphrased) (the Duchy of Rome, a Byzantine administrative division). The core is Rome and Lazio.

region.text: the exarchate of Ravenna and the five cities of the Pentapolis (Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia, Ancona)

ledger.note: 756: the exarchate of Ravenna and the Pentapolis pass to the pope. After the second Frankish campaign (April 756) Aistulf gave hostages, agreed to annual tribute and promised in writing to return the occupied territories (page, paraphrased); the keys of the cities were placed on the altar of Old St Peter's. The page names Ravenna, Rimini, Pesaro, Fano, Senigallia, Ancona and Forlì; boundaries 'can only be approximated'.

region.text: the Lombard ducatus ferrariae

ledger.note: 757: the Lombard duchy of Ferrara pledged to the pope. Desiderius pledged the Lombard 'ducatus ferrariae' to Pope Stephen II (page, paraphrased). A pledge, not a possession: Cliopatria's shape adds Bologna, Imola and Ferrara only in 763.

region.text: Bologna, Imola and Ferrara added to the Cliopatria shape in 763

ledger.note: 763: Emilia (Bologna, Imola, Ferrara) joins the shape. Page silent: the Ferrara page dates only the 757 pledge and the Donation page says the Lombard conquests in Romagna were included; 763 is Cliopatria's shape year.

region.text: the exarchate, the Pentapolis and Emilia, taken out of the drawn shape in 775

ledger.note: 775: the shape withdraws to the Duchy of Rome after Charlemagne is king of the Lombards. Page silent on a loss: Charlemagne besieged Pavia in 774 and received the title of King of the Lombards (page, paraphrased); the Donation was confirmed by Charlemagne in 778 (page, paraphrased), so the exarchate stays a claim while effective control is drawn only in Lazio (Romagna page: papal control 'only nominal').

region.text: the strip of southern Tuscany added to the shape in 783

ledger.note: 781: Charlemagne's reputed extension of papal lands. 'Some later claimed that in 781' he extended papal lands to include Ravenna, the Pentapolis, parts of Benevento, Tuscany, Corsica and Lombardy; the page treats it as a later claim. Cliopatria's 783 shape adds a southern Tuscan strip; the claimed Romagna lands stay out of the drawn shape.

region.text: the Tuscan strip reduced in the 793 shape

ledger.note: 793: the shape shrinks by about 5,000 km2. Page silent: no page opened explains it; Cliopatria's year.

region.text: the March of Ancona (Ancona, Fermo, Macerata, Camerino, Ascoli, Osimo, Urbino)

ledger.note: 1198: Innocent III's papacy acquires the March of Ancona. The March 'definitely acquired by the Papal States during the pontificate of Innocent III in the year 1198'; in 1177 Alexander III had called it 'partly belonging to the empire but largely to the church'. Governed by papal rectors; capital Fermo from 1210.

region.text: Ferrara and its domains, about 1,100 km2 south of the lower Po

ledger.note: 1208: the Este become lords of Ferrara under the pope. 'In 1208, Azzo VI d'Este became seignior of Ferrara'; Ferrara 'formally part of the Papal States', so the Este were papal vassals. Azzo VIII died in 1308 and Clement V tried to take direct rule, but Robert of Naples governed for nine years before the Este were recalled in 1317 (Papal States page); not drawn separately.

region.text: Spoleto, Perugia, Terni, Rieti, Gubbio and the southern Marche added in Cliopatria's 1272 shape

ledger.note: 1272: Umbria joins the shape. Page silent: no page opened dates the papal hold on the Duchy of Spoleto, Perugia, Terni, Rieti and Gubbio; 1272 is Cliopatria's shape year.

region.text: the Comtat Venaissin, between the Rhône, the Durance and Mont Ventoux

ledger.note: 1274: the Comtat Venaissin becomes papal territory, a detached dependency in Provence. The Comtat 'became a Papal territory in 1274' (Alphonse of Poitiers 'bequeathed it to the Holy See on his death in 1271'); governed by a rector, capital Venasque, from 1320 Carpentras. Drawn as a dependency tint because Cliopatria keeps it as its own row.

region.text: Romagna, with Bologna, Ferrara, Ancona and Urbino in Cliopatria's 1279 shape

ledger.note: 1278: Rudolf I cedes Romagna. 'King Rudolf I of Germany officially ceded Romagna to the Papal States in 1278'; 'papal control over the area long remained only nominal' (lords such as the Ordelaffi of Forlì and the Malatesta of Rimini). Cliopatria's 1279 shape adds Romagna with Bologna, Ferrara, Ancona and Urbino; only Romagna is named by the page.
1309: the court moves to Avignon. The infobox gives the capital as 'Rome (756-1308; 1376-1870)' and Avignon '(1309-1376)'; the text dates the Avignon papacy 'From 1305 to 1378'.

region.text: the city of Avignon

ledger.note: 1348: the popes buy Avignon. Avignon 'was sold to the papacy by Joanna I' in 1348; the two comtats formed one enclave with separate political identities.

1376: the papacy returns to Rome (infobox 'Rome 1376-1870'); the page's text dates the end of the Avignon papacy to 1378 and Albornoz's restoration of papal control to the Constitutiones Aegidianae of 29 April 1357.

region.text: Romagna: Ravenna, Forlì, Cesena and Rimini

ledger.note: 1500: Cesare Borgia carves out the Duchy of Romagna. In 1500 Cesare Borgia 'carved out for himself an ephemeral Duchy of Romagna' (page) under his father Alexander VI (the pope is the researcher's reading of the Julius II page).

region.text: Romagna: Ravenna, Forlì, Cesena and Rimini

ledger.note: 1503: the Duchy of Romagna falls with the Borgia. Page silent on the year: After Alexander VI died, his lands were taken by Pope Julius II (Romagna page, no year) and Cesare 'shared the same fate' and 'lost his possessions' after Julius's election (Julius II page, no date).

region.text: Bologna and Perugia

ledger.counterpart: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia
ledger.note: 1506: Julius II marches on Bologna and Perugia. He 'personally led the 1506 campaign that freed Perugia and Bologna from their despots, Gian Paolo Baglioni and Giovanni II Bentivoglio'; the Bologna campaign ran from 17 August 1506.

region.text: Bologna and Perugia

ledger.counterpart: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia
ledger.note: 1507: the despots are gone. The Bologna campaign ended on 23 March 1507 and Perugia 'voluntarily surrendered' in March 1507. Bologna was lost again from 27 June 1511 to March 1512 (the page only says the pope mourned 'the loss of the city of Bologna'); not drawn.

region.text: the western edge added in Cliopatria's 1507 shape

ledger.counterpart: Bentivoglio of Bologna and Baglioni of Perugia
ledger.note: 1507: Cliopatria's shape widens by about 1,050 km2 on its western edge (to 10.86 E, towards Modena and the Bologna hills), the year the Bologna campaign ended (23 March 1507). Page silent: no page opened names the land; the Julius II page says only that Bologna and Perugia were freed from their despots.

region.text: the Romagna coast taken by Venice: Faenza, Rimini and other towns

ledger.note: 1509: the pope and the League of Cambrai against Venice in Romagna. 'In May 1509, Julius sent troops against Venetian forces that had occupied parts of Romagna', aiming to expel Venice from Faenza, Rimini and other towns; the League was formed in December 1508.

region.text: the Romagna coast taken by Venice: Faenza, Rimini and other towns

ledger.note: 1509: Agnadello leads to the recovery of Romagna. The battle of Agnadello of 14 May 1509 led to the papal recovery of territory (paraphrased); the page does not date the recovery of Faenza, Rimini or Ravenna, and Venice was absolved at the beginning of 1510.

region.text: Parma and Piacenza

ledger.note: 1512: Parma and Piacenza fall to the pope. In May 1512 Julius hired Swiss mercenaries against the French in Milan and the papacy then gained control of Parma and Piacenza (paraphrased); the Congress of Mantua (1512) annexed Parma and Modena (page, undated). Counterpart Milan is the researcher's reading; the page does not name the previous holder.

region.text: Parma and Piacenza

ledger.note: 1545: Parma and Piacenza become a duchy for Paul III's son. In 1545 Parma and Piacenza became a duchy under an illegitimate son of Paul III (page, paraphrased). A papal fief, no longer drawn as direct papal land.

region.text: Ferrara and its domains

ledger.note: 1597: the main Este line dies out. 'When Alfonso died in 1597, he had no legitimate male heir'; Clement VIII did not acknowledge Cesare d'Este's succession and treated Ferrara as a vacant papal fief.

region.text: the Duchy of Ferrara and Comacchio

ledger.note: 1597: the pope takes Ferrara and Comacchio. the page states the Papal States took Ferrara in 1597 (Duchy of Ferrara page; the Romagna page also gives 1597; the Papal States page dates the reclaim 1598); Comacchio was claimed the same way; the Este kept Modena and Reggio.

region.text: the Duchy of Urbino

ledger.note: 1631: the Duchy of Urbino is reclaimed. The Papal States page says the duchy was reclaimed that year (paraphrased). Cliopatria's shapes already include Urbino from 1279, so the gain moves no cells in the shape (notes).

region.text: the Duchy of Castro

ledger.note: 1649: the Duchy of Castro is annexed. 'In 1649, after the annexation of the Duchy of Castro, the Papal States reached their greatest extent.'

region.text: the Comtat Venaissin and Avignon

ledger.note: 1768: French troops occupy the Comtat Venaissin and Avignon. The text says the region 'was invaded by French troops in 1663, 1668 and 1768-1774'; only the last span is given as a span, and the earlier invasions are not drawn.

region.text: the Comtat Venaissin and Avignon

ledger.note: 1774: the French occupation of the Comtat and Avignon ends (the page gives the span 1768-1774).

region.text: the Comtat Venaissin

ledger.note: 14 September 1791: the Comtat votes to join France. 'An unauthorized plebiscite, under pressure from French revolutionaries' was held and the inhabitants voted for annexation; the papacy did not recognise it 'until 1814'. The Treaty of Tolentino (1797) 'formally ceded' both to France and the Congress of Vienna did not return them (Papal States page).

region.text: the city of Avignon

ledger.note: 14 September 1791: Avignon goes with the Comtat to revolutionary France.

region.text: the Legations of Bologna, Ferrara, Ravenna and Forlì

ledger.note: 1796: the French seize the Legations. After the Armistice of Bologna (21 million lire demanded) the Legations were seized by the French and became part of the Cispadane Republic (Papal States page, paraphrased); in February 1797 9,000 French soldiers invaded the Papal Romagna (Tolentino page).

region.text: the Legations of Bologna, Ferrara, Ravenna and Forlì

ledger.note: February 1797: the occupation of the Legations becomes a cession. The Treaty of Tolentino was 'signed on 19 February 1797'.

region.text: Romagna, Ferrara and Bologna, the Papal Legations

ledger.note: 19 February 1797: Tolentino strips the Legations. Romagna, Ferrara and Bologna 'were also ceded by the Papal States and incorporated into the newly created Cispadane Republic'; Avignon and the Comtat 'formally ceded to France'; the pope consents to French troops in Ancona 'until the end of the war'. The indemnity was 36 million livres in total (Tolentino page; the Papal States page says a further 30 million lire).

region.text: the remaining papal state, Rome and Lazio, Umbria and the Marche

ledger.note: 15 February 1798: Rome becomes a republic. Berthier 'occupied Rome on 11 February 1798' and the republic 'was proclaimed on 15 February 1798'; Pius VI was escorted out on 20 February; the republic 'immediately incorporated' the Tiberina and Anconine republics.

region.text: the restored state, without the Legations

ledger.note: June 1800: the Papal States are restored. The Papal States page: the French Consulate restored the Papal States and Pius VII took residence in Rome (page, paraphrased); the Roman Republic page: 'restored under the rule of Pope Pius VII in June 1800' (its lead says October 1799 after a second Neapolitan invasion of 30 September 1799).

region.text: Urbino, Ancona, Macerata and Camerino

ledger.note: 2 April 1808: the Marche go to Napoleon's Kingdom of Italy. Napoleon annexed Urbino, Ancona, Macerata and Camerino to the Kingdom of Italy (page, paraphrased).

region.text: Lazio and Umbria, the rest of the state with Rome

ledger.note: 17 May 1809: Rome is annexed to the French Empire. The rest of the state, including Rome, was annexed to the First French Empire (Schönbrunn Palace Declarations, 17 May 1809); the pope was in exile 1809-1814 (Papal Legations page).

region.text: the restored state

ledger.note: 1814: the Papal States are restored. The infobox dates the post-Napoleonic monarchy from 1814, and the Congress of Vienna of 1814-15 restored the Italian territories but not the Comtat Venaissin or Avignon (page, paraphrased); the Papal Legations page: in 1815 the Congress of Vienna restored the Papal State. The Marche and Legations came back from the Kingdom of Italy; the page does not date each.

region.text: the Papal States held by the Roman Republic

ledger.note: 9 February 1849: the Roman Republic is proclaimed. The Constitutional Assembly proclaimed the Roman Republic after midnight on 9 February (page, paraphrased) after Pius IX left for Gaeta on 24 November 1848; the page lists no territories and speaks only of the Papal States and Roman territory generally (paraphrased).

region.text: the Papal States restored

ledger.note: 3 July 1849: French troops end the Roman Republic. the French Army entered Rome on 3 July 1849 and re-established the Holy See's temporal power (page, paraphrased); Pius IX returned in April 1850 (a 'Red Triumvirate' of cardinals governed until then); French soldiers who had propped up the papal administration stayed until 1870 (page, paraphrased).

region.text: Bologna, Ferrara, Forlì and Ravenna, the Papal Legations

ledger.note: 1859: the Legations break away. the Kingdom of Sardinia invaded the Papal State and set up a military government, the United Provinces of Central Italy, which included the Romagne (Papal Legations page, paraphrased); in December 1859 Tuscany formed a union with Modena, Parma and the Papal Legations (United Provinces page, paraphrased); annexed to Sardinia after the 11 March 1860 vote.

region.text: the Marche and Umbria

ledger.note: 11 September 1860: Sardinia invades the Marche and Umbria. After a 7 September ultimatum, 'the Sardinian army crossed the border on 11 September'; Castelfidardo 18 September 1860.

region.text: Ancona

ledger.note: 29 September 1860: Ancona surrenders to Sardinia after the siege that followed Castelfidardo.

region.text: the Marche and Umbria

ledger.note: November 1860: the Marche and Umbria vote to join Sardinia. 'In November 1860, plebiscites were held in the Marche and Umbria' and led to annexation; the Papal States page: 'Bologna, Ferrara, Umbria, the Marches, Benevento and Pontecorvo' were annexed by November 1860.

region.text: the Marche and Umbria

ledger.note: November 1860: the fighting over the Marche and Umbria ends in annexation.

region.text: Lazio, the last papal territory

ledger.note: 11 September 1870: the Italian army enters the Papal States. 'Italian troops led by General Raffaele Cadorna entered the Papal States with the objective of taking Rome'; Civitavecchia was occupied on 16 September; the French garrison had been recalled in early August.

region.text: Lazio, the last papal territory

ledger.note: 20 September 1870: Porta Pia. 'The Italian army breached the Aurelian Walls near Porta Pia'; the capitulation was signed at Villa Albani.

region.text: Rome and Lazio, annexed to the Kingdom of Italy

ledger.note: 20 September 1870: Rome falls and the Papal States end. The capture 'brought an end to the Papal States', which had existed since the Donation of Pepin in 756; 2 October plebiscite (133,681 for union, 1,507 against), royal decree of 9 October 1870; the Leonine City was left to Pius IX; Law of Guarantees 13 May 1871, Vatican City 11 February 1929.

wars.name: Frankish campaigns against the Lombards (Pepin and Aistulf)

zones.text: the exarchate of Ravenna and the Pentapolis

wars.outcome: Pepin crossed Mont Cenis in spring 755 and beat the Lombards near Susa (First Peace of Pavia); Aistulf besieged Rome from 1 January 756; a second Frankish army in April 756 forced the Second Peace of Pavia, with hostages, tribute and a written promise to return the occupied territories. The Donation of Pepin followed in 756.

wars.name: Frankish conquest of the Lombard kingdom
wars.outcome: Hadrian I asked for help against the Lombards; Charlemagne besieged Pavia in 774 and took the title King of the Lombards after Desiderius surrendered. The Donation was confirmed by Charlemagne in 778 (page) and Louis the Pious in 817.

wars.name: Cesare Borgia's conquest of Romagna
belligerents: Lords of Romagna (Ordelaffi, Malatesta and others)
wars.outcome: Cesare Borgia carved out an ephemeral Duchy of Romagna in 1500; after Alexander VI died his lands were taken by Julius II.
wars.note: The Romagna page gives no end year; 1503 is bridged from Julius II's election (confidence 1).

wars.name: Julius II's campaign against Bologna and Perugia
wars.outcome: The pope personally led the campaign (Bologna, 17 August 1506 to 23 March 1507) that freed Perugia and Bologna from their despots; Perugia 'voluntarily surrendered' in March 1507.

wars.name: War of the League of Cambrai (papal front in Romagna)
wars.outcome: The League was formed in December 1508; Julius sent troops in May 1509 against Venetian forces in Romagna, and Agnadello (14 May 1509) led, per the page, to the papal recovery of territory. Venice was absolved at the beginning of 1510.

wars.name: Julius II's war for Ferrara and the Holy League
wars.outcome: Julius's attempt to recover Ferrara ran from 1 September 1510 to 29 June 1512 (the page does not state the outcome; Ferrara was taken only in 1597); the Holy League was created on 4 October 1511; Louis XII won at Ravenna on 11 April 1512; in May 1512 the papacy gained control of Parma and Piacenza.

wars.name: Italian War of 1551-1559 (papal part)
wars.outcome: Philip II's armies defeated Paul IV's (Papal States page, paraphrased); no border moved. The Romagna page adds that in 1559 the Peace of Cateau-Cambresis 'divided Romagna between the Farnese family' and others and the Papal States, without detail.

wars.name: Sack of Rome (1527)
belligerents: Charles V (Holy Roman Empire and Spain)
wars.outcome: Troops loyal to Charles V sacked Rome and imprisoned Clement VII; no border moved.

wars.name: French invasion of the Papal States (1796-1797)

zones.text: the Legations of Bologna, Ferrara and Romagna

wars.outcome: The Armistice of Bologna (1796) cost 21 million lire; the French seized the Legations; in February 1797 9,000 French soldiers invaded Papal Romagna and the pope accepted the Treaty of Tolentino of 19 February 1797, ceding Romagna, Ferrara and Bologna and Avignon with the Comtat.

wars.name: Neapolitan invasions of the Roman Republic
wars.outcome: The French occupied Rome on 11 February 1798 and proclaimed the republic on 15 February; Naples invaded in November 1798 (entering Rome unopposed on 29 November, beaten at Civita Castellana on 5 December and Otricoli on 9 December, French back in Rome on 14 December) and again on 30 September 1799; the Papal States were restored in June 1800 (October 1799 according to the page's lead).

wars.name: Napoleonic annexation of the Papal States
wars.outcome: The Marche were annexed to the Kingdom of Italy on 2 April 1808; the rest, with Rome, to the First French Empire on 17 May 1809.

wars.name: Roman Republic and the French intervention of 1849
wars.outcome: Oudinot landed 8,000 to 10,000 French at Civitavecchia on 25 April 1849; the siege of Rome began in earnest on 1 June; the French entered Rome on 3 July 1849 and re-established the pope's temporal power; Garibaldi withdrew to San Marino on 2 July. Spain sent 4,000 men to Gaeta and Neapolitan troops entered the republic's territory.

wars.name: Sardinian invasion of the Papal States (1860)
wars.outcome: Ultimatum 7 September, invasion 11 September, Castelfidardo 18 September, Ancona surrendered 29 September; plebiscites in the Marche and Umbria in November 1860 gave their annexation to Sardinia.

wars.name: Capture of Rome (1870)
wars.outcome: The French garrison was recalled in early August 1870; Italian troops crossed the frontier on 11 September, occupied Civitavecchia on 16 September, reached the walls on 19 September and breached them at Porta Pia on 20 September 1870; plebiscite 2 October and decree of 9 October 1870.

certainty.note: The Patrimony around Rome is firm; the exarchate, the Marche and Romagna were held through papal vicars and lords, and the Romagna page says papal control 'long remained only nominal'. Ferrara (Este) and the Comtat are fiefs and dependencies.

Pius IV established a specific identification for each province in 1559-1565 and a Congregation for Borders (1627) mediated jurisdictional disputes (Papal States page); the enclaves of Benevento, Pontecorvo, Avignon and the Comtat have their own lines.
French occupations, republics and annexations changed the lines almost yearly; no treaty line holds.
Restored by the Congress of Vienna; the frontier with the Kingdom of Sardinia and the Two Sicilies follows treaty lines until the 1859-60 and 1870 annexations.

notes:
PAPAL STATES 756-1870, eu-13-d. All 14 pages of the budget were spent (Papal States, Donation of Pepin, March of Ancona, Romagna, Comtat Venaissin, Duchy of Ferrara, Treaty of Tolentino, Roman Republic (18th century), Roman Republic (1849), United Provinces of Central Italy, Papal Legations, Battle of Castelfidardo, Capture of Rome, Pope Julius II). WebFetch returned summaries of each page, with quotes under about 125 characters; the notes quote only what the tool returned in quotation marks.

ONE STATE, NOT SPLIT. Cliopatria's single row 755-1870 is one continuous state in the Wikipedia article (infobox: 'under the direct sovereign rule of the pope from 756 to 1870'). The two breaks (Roman Republic February 1798 to June 1800; annexation to the Kingdom of Italy and the French Empire 1808-1814) are drawn as loss/gain events, not as new states; the colour and dossier continue. The state starts in 756 (Cliopatria 755) and ends 20 September 1870 (Capture of Rome).

CLIOPATRIA ROWS TO CORRECT (all in keyframe_review): 755 shape drawn from 756 only; 1147 and 1202-1272 shapes lack the March of Ancona acquired in 1198; 1507-1555 shapes lack Parma and Piacenza (1512-1545, new keyframe 1512 and verdicts on 1507 and 1529); 1600-1796 shapes lack the Duchy of Castro (1649, new keyframe 1649 and adjust verdicts); 1800-1802 shape wrongly includes the Legations ceded in 1797; 1797 shape drawn for 1797 only (Roman Republic from 15 February 1798, no papal state until June 1800); 1807 shape for 1807 only with a new keyframe for 1808 (Marche annexed 2 April 1808; rest 17 May 1809); 1859 shape without the Legations. Relation rows: the allegiance of the Papal States to the Byzantine Empire 755-869 is contradicted by the Donation of Pepin page (the Empire's envoys offered money to restore the lands, Pepin refused, 'the imperial presence in central Italy' was at an end); the alliance with the Spanish Empire 1564-1611 is not territory. Ledger events override the shape in their year; the vassal tints (Ferrara 1208-1597, Comtat Venaissin 1274-1791, Romagna under Cesare Borgia 1500-1503) sit inside or beside the Cliopatria outline and the renderer should let the tint win.

NOT SETTLED (page silent or page budget):
- Rulers: the ruler strip needs the 'List of popes' page; not opened, so identity.rulers is omitted.
- Native names ('Stato Pontificio', 'Stato della Chiesa') are not read from a page.
- 775-1271: Cliopatria draws only the Patrimony in Lazio; the pages say the exarchate and Pentapolis stayed a claim (Charlemagne's confirmation in 778 per the Donation page, an extension 'some later claimed' for 781 per the Papal States page) and that Romagna control was 'only nominal'. The 775 and 793 losses and the 1272 Umbria gain are confidence 1 (shape years, no page). How and when the Duchy of Spoleto, Perugia, Rieti and Terni became papal is not on any page opened.
- Bologna: the Julius II page calls Bentivoglio a despot in 1506; the earlier signorie (Visconti, Pepoli) and the 1511 loss (27 June 1511 to March 1512) are not dated beyond that.
- Marche and Romagna 1198-1500: governed by rectors and local lords (Malatesta, Ordelaffi, Da Varano and others); the pages give no dates for individual lordships.
- Urbino: Cliopatria draws the duchy inside the shape from 1279; the Papal States page says it was reclaimed in 1631. The ledger records the 1631 gain at confidence 3 but the shape is not corrected for 1279-1630 because no page dates when Urbino became a fief. A gap-filler should open 'Duchy of Urbino'.
- Benevento and Pontecorvo: described as southern enclaves and listed as annexed by Sardinia by November 1860 (Papal States page), but no page opened dates the acquisition (the duchy-of-benevento dossier has 1053 and 1081 events from other pages) and the Napoleonic principalities of 1806 are not on any page. Not in the ledger.
- Modena (annexed 1512 according to the Julius II page, undated; not Reggio) is not drawn.
- The Austrian occupation of Bologna, Ferrara and Ancona (1849-1859) and the French garrison in Rome (1849-1870) are not on the pages opened as dated occupations; only that French soldiers who had propped up the papal administration stayed until 1870 (Roman Republic 1849 page, paraphrased) and the Papal Legations page's silence on both.
- 1859: the June risings in Bologna and Romagna and the departure of the legate are not on the United Provinces or Papal Legations pages; the loss is dated by year only (December 1859 for the union).
- 1814-1815: whether the Marche and the Legations were back in 1814 or only in 1815 (Congress of Vienna) is not said; the 1814 gain and shape are therefore confidence 2 / unverified.
- 962 Diploma Ottonianum, the Donation of Matilda, the Treaty of Venice (1177 is on the Papal States page but moved no border), Innocent III's recovery beyond 1198, Frederick II, the Avignon-period losses and Albornoz's reconquest (29 April 1357 Constitutiones) have no territorial events because no page opened dates a border change.

CONFLICTS BETWEEN PAGES (resolved in the ledger as stated): Ferrara taken in 1597 (Duchy of Ferrara, Romagna pages) or 1598 (Papal States page): 1597 used. Papal States restored June 1800 (Roman Republic body, Papal States page) or October 1799 (Roman Republic lead): June 1800 used. French entry into Rome 11 February 1798 (text) or 15 February (image caption): both given. Tolentino indemnity 36 million livres in all (Tolentino page) or a further 30 million lire (Papal States page). Charlemagne's confirmation 778 (Donation page) or 781 (Papal States page, as a later claim). Avignon papacy 1309-1376 (infobox) or 1305-1378 (text). United Provinces annexed 22 March 1860 (infobox) or voted 11 March and presented to Parliament 12 April (text). French entry into Rome 3 July 1849 (page; some accounts say 4 July).

COUNTERPARTS NEEDING DOSSIERS: duchy-of-ferrara (Este, 1208?-1597), duchy-of-urbino (to 1631), duchy-of-castro (Farnese, to 1649), duchy-of-romagna (Cesare Borgia 1500-1503), duchy-of-parma-and-piacenza (Farnese duchy from 1545; the Cliopatria row is 1815-1859), roman-republic-1849 (9 February to 3 July 1849), revolutionary-roman-republic (Cliopatria row 1799 only; the republic ran 15 February 1798 to autumn 1799 or June 1800), united-provinces-of-central-italy (1859-1860), and the Napoleonic Kingdom of Italy (1805-1814), which the ledger names italian-republic (the Cliopatria row 1803-1813) for the 1808 annexation of the Marche. kingdom-of-france, comtat-venaissin, kingdom-of-the-lombards, exarchate-of-ravenna, byzantine-empire and capetian-house-of-anjou have dossiers or Cliopatria rows already.

GAZETTEER: all region names resolve (Marche, Umbria, Latium, Comtat Venaissin; admin1 Ravenna, Forlì-Cesena, Rimini, Bologna, Ferrara, Parma, Piacenza, Pesaro e Urbino; places Rome, Avignon, Ferrara, Comacchio, Bologna, Perugia, Ancona). The Duchy of Castro is a 25 km disc at 11.74 E, 42.54 N (Ischia di Castro) because the gazetteer has no historical region for it; the Legations are a union of the four provinces plus Rimini. A gazetteer entry 'Duchy of Castro' and 'Romagna' (region) would be better.
